To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Shas, a religious movement of Oriental Jews, has established a religious educational system that challenges secular national identity in Israel.
the Shas educational stream was established to respond to the educational needs of the Sephardic population in Israel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which religious movements and ethnic groups use education to create and sustain their own cultural spheres.
how religious groups use educational systems to foster social mobilization, and to promote a new religious ethnic identity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rise of the religious education system in Israel is a response to the social and political needs of a religious ethnic minority that is marginalized and discriminated against.
Shas's educational system is a response to the needs and interests of a population that is excluded and marginalized from the national project.
Shas education system is a case study for the transformation of religious movements into a political force.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Shas's educational system is an example of a religious movement's ability to embrace education and to transform the cultural boundaries and norms that are inherent in modem systems of mass schooling.
Shas's education system, by creating a new cultural sphere, is contributing to the formation of an Ultra Orthodox Israeli Jewish identity.

the new religious educational system is a social movement that is able to create and maintain a new cultural sphere and identity, by using education as a tool to mobilize the group and to create solidarity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
religious groups can use education to create and sustain a sense of collective identity and to promote social and political mobilization.

the religious educational system is not a monolithic entity, but rather is comprised of a variety of sub-systems, each with its unique goals and practices, and that it is the interaction between the different sub-systems that makes this system so complex.

the religious revival in Israel is not a simple revival of religious values, but a complex process of cultural change and social reorganization that has profound implications for the educational system.
